title: add-provenance-anchors-and-version-notary-workflow
author: Priya Singh
description:
Motivation: onboarding workflows currently lack compact, verifiable provenance snippets and a lightweight version notarization step that ties a model upload to deterministic metadata and a stable version token. This PR introduces 'provenance anchors' (compact signed fingerprints derived from model manifest + sample telemetry) and a 'version notary' service that issues short canonical version tokens and generates a succinct release blurb suitable for changelogs and automated release notes.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a provenance anchor generator (tools/anchor_generator.py) that canonicalizes manifest fields, computes a content-hash, and attaches sampled telemetry signatures to improve de-dup and drift detection. 2) Introduces a notary microservice (notary/service.py) that consumes anchors and returns an immutable version token (vtoken) together with a short humanized summary used by release automation. 3) Plumbs anchor metadata into the onboarding pipeline (ingest/worker.py changes) so every successful model intake stores anchor and vtoken in the model index. 4) Adds a changelog helper (scripts/brief_builder.py) that converts vtoken + anchor into a one-paragraph release note draft and a compact manifest excerpt for audits. 5) Tests for anchor stability and notary idempotency (tests/test_anchor.py, tests/test_notary_idempotency.py). 6) CI pipeline updates to run anchor stability matrix on a sample of previously onboarded models.

Design notes: - Anchors are intentionally compact (<= 256 bytes) and include: canonical manifest hash, sampled latency/quantile telemetry fingerprint, and a short provenance salt. Anchors are signed using the existing keystore integration so they can be verified offline. - The vtoken is a short base32 token (8-10 chars) derived from the signed anchor fingerprint; it is intended for human-friendly usage (UIs, changelogs) and is not a replacement for full model versioning semantics. - Notary enforces idempotency: repeated submissions with identical canonical manifest -> same vtoken. Different telemetry samples will be canonicalized into the anchor deterministically. - The changelog helper emits an opinionated short blurb: model alias, vtoken, delta hints (new/changed inputs), and a single-line cost/perf note if telemetry delta > threshold.

Checklist: - [x] Anchor generator implementation + unit tests
- [x] Notary service + integration tests
- [x] Pipeline integration (worker commit) + warmup hooks
- [x] Changelog helper + template
- [x] CI stability matrix job
- [x] Docs: docs/provenance_anchors.md + examples in redwood-examples repo (link added)

Testing & validation: ran anchor stability suite against 120 model manifests (2/14/2025 sample) and verified bit-stable anchors after canonicalization. Notary idempotency tested with 50 repeated uploads. CI job includes an expanded sample check that previously failed once (flaky serialization) and was fixed by normalizing timestamp fields.

Rollout plan: feature-gated by config flag model_registry.enable_provenance_anchors (default off). We'll rollout to staging for 48 hours, run a smoke ingestion of the nightly model-catalog and verify anchors and vtoken generation. After monitoring (console dashboard widget added), toggle on in production. Backout: disable flag and purge vtoken index writes (safe no-destructive path).

Security & compliance: Keystore usage relies on existing KMS integration; signing keys are rotated per current rotation policy. No sensitive telemetry is included — only aggregated sample hashes and quantiles. Compliance reviewed by Security (SUP-1282) and accepted with minor doc clarifications.

Related work: builds on prior intake normalization work (ENG-3780) and the changelog autobuilder prototype (ENG-4602).

review_comments: Luca Romano (2025-02-15): Nice compact representation. Small request: can we avoid including raw quantile arrays in the anchor payload? Suggest storing a hash of the quantile vector instead so the anchor stays tightly bounded.
Author (Priya) (2025-02-15): Good catch — switched quantile vector to a SHA256 of the vector and updated tests. Anchors are still verifiable with the hash plus signature.
Maya Chen (2025-02-16): Security reviewed the keystore usage; confirm rotation semantics. Also please add a note about rate limits for the notary to avoid accidental floods during bulk backfills.
Author (Priya) (2025-02-16): Added keystore doc links and a circuit-breaker to notary/service.py; rate limit default is 500 reqs/min per api-key. Added to docs and config.

Diego Alvarez (2025-02-17): Integration test failed once due to nondeterministic JSON ordering in example manifests. Recommend adding a deterministic serializer — either canonical JSON or stable field ordering.
Author (Priya) (2025-02-17): Implemented deterministic serializer using sorted keys and explicit field whitelist. Re-ran stability matrix; all green.
ci_details: Initial CI run: failed (serialization flake) -> pushed deterministic serializer fix -> subsequent CI run: pass. New CI job 'anchor_stability_matrix' added; runs nightly against sampled manifests. Full pipeline green on merge. Logs attached to PR run #1423.
release_notes: Introduce provenance anchors: compact, signed fingerprints tying model manifest + sampled telemetry into a short verifiable anchor.
Add version notary that issues stable human-friendly vtokens for use in UI and changelogs.
Pipeline integration so newly onboarded models record anchor + vtoken in the model index (feature-gated).
New changelog brief builder that converts vtoken + anchor into a one-paragraph automated release note draft.
CI: anchor stability matrix job added to nightly checks.
